questions.question: Give the three Spaulding classifications, state the level of processing (sterilization/disinfection) required for each, and give one example of each.

parts.text: Give the three Spaulding classes, the required level of processing for each, and one example of each.

parts_raw.text: Three Spaulding classifications and sterilization for each.  One example of each type.

questions.model_answer: (1) Critical items – contact sterile tissue or the vascular system; require sterilization (preferably steam; if heat/moisture sensitive, ETO, hydrogen peroxide gas plasma/vapour, or a liquid chemical sterilant); e.g. surgical instruments, implants, biopsy forceps. (2) Semicritical items – contact intact mucous membranes or nonintact skin; require high-level disinfection (e.g. glutaraldehyde, OPA); e.g. gastrointestinal endoscopes, bronchoscopes. (3) Noncritical items – contact intact skin only; require low-level (or intermediate-level) disinfection; e.g. blood pressure cuffs, bed rails.

cohort_answer.text: Spaulding classification - rational approach to disinfection and sterilization of patient care items. Critical items - high risk of infection if contaminated with any organism, e.g. surgical instruments, cardiac or urinary catheters, implants, ultrasound probes in sterile body cavities; sterilize with steam or liquid chemical sterilants if heat sensitive. Semicritical items - contact mucous membranes or non-intact skin, e.g. endoscopes, laryngoscope blades, esophageal manometry probes, cystoscopes; usually high level disinfection with chemicals. Non-critical items - contact with intact skin and not mucous membranes.

questions.question: Infection prevention and control audited the GI clinic and found that some of the time the endoscopes are not brushed off and cleaned prior to disinfection with glutaraldehyde.
questions.question_raw: IPAC has made routine investigations in the GI clinic and has found that some of the time, the endoscopes are not brushed off and cleaned prior to disinfection with glutaraldehyde.

parts.text: What are two breaches that have occurred in the GI clinic?
List three Spaulding criteria and the level of disinfection/sterilization for each class.

parts_raw.text: What are 2 breaches that have occurred in the GI clinic?
List 3 spaulding criteria and the level of disinfection/sterilization for each class.

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Internal channels were not brushed before disinfection – mechanical brushing of all accessible channels is a mandatory first step; residual organic soil/biofilm shields organisms and prevents the disinfectant from contacting and killing them. (2) The scope was not cleaned/flushed with an enzymatic detergent before immersion – high-level disinfection is validated only on a mechanically cleaned device, so omitting cleaning invalidates the disinfection. b) (1) Critical – contact sterile tissue/vascular system → sterilization (e.g. surgical instruments, implants). (2) Semicritical – contact intact mucous membranes/nonintact skin → high-level disinfection (e.g. GI endoscopes, bronchoscopes). (3) Noncritical – contact intact skin only → low-level disinfection (e.g. blood pressure cuff, bed rail).
questions.cohort_conflict: The cohort listed "glutaraldehyde not appropriate" as a possible breach; per Mandell glutaraldehyde is an accepted high-level disinfectant/chemical sterilant for endoscopes, so its use is not a breach – the breaches lie in the omitted brushing/cleaning.

cohort_answer.text: Not cleaning prior to disinfection; ?glutaraldehyde not appropriate for disinfection. || Critical: equipment that enters sterile body spaces - cleaning + sterilization, e.g. surgical equipment, implants, eye/dental equipment. Semi-critical: equipment that comes into contact with mucous membranes/non-intact skin but doesn't penetrate them - cleaning + high level disinfection (sterilization preferred), e.g. anaesthesia/resp equipment. Non-critical: equipment that comes into contact with intact skin or doesn't directly contact patient/mucous membranes - cleaning + low level disinfection (sometimes cleaning alone is ok), e.g. ECG machine, oximeter, commode.

questions.model_answer: (1) Critical – e.g. surgical instruments (or implants, biopsy forceps). (2) Semicritical – e.g. gastrointestinal endoscope (or bronchoscope, laryngoscope). (3) Noncritical – e.g. blood pressure cuff (or bed rail, bedpan).

cohort_answer.text: Sterilization: destroys/eliminates all forms of microbial life (steam under pressure, dry heat, EtO gas, hydrogen peroxide gas plasma, liquid chemicals). Disinfection: eliminates many/all pathogenic microorganisms except bacterial spores (liquid chemicals or wet pasteurization). Cleaning: removal of visible soil, manually or mechanically with water/detergents/enzymatic products; decontamination removes pathogenic microorganisms so objects are safe to handle
